assessment.nobel_worthiness: Transformative: incretin physiology (GLP-1 secretion, insulinotropic action, trophic and satiety effects) translated into a drug class that changes treatment of type 2 diabetes, obesity and cardiometabolic outcomes. Clear, original, and of very large and growing impact on patients.
assessment.attribution: Credit is distributed among Holst (physiology and GLP-1 biology), Mojsov (peptide identification and synthesis, contested priority), Drucker (preproglucagon and GLP-2/GLP-1 biology, therapeutic rationale) and Knudsen (industrial development of liraglutide/semaglutide). A three-person prize around the physiological discovery is plausible, but the three-name limit forces exclusion of Knudsen.
assessment.maturity: Mature in efficacy with multiple large randomized outcome trials and global clinical use; timing is excellent, though long-term safety and some mechanisms (central actions) are still being clarified.
uncertainties: Priority and credit dispute around Mojsov and the peptide characterization
Whether the prize should recognize the physiology or the drug development, and how to include Knudsen
Long-term safety and mechanistic details remain under study

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells redirected against tumour antigens produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukaemia and lymphoma, establishing a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) with strong conceptual originality.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulation and second-generation CAR design), June (clinical translation and CD19 CAR-T trials), Rosenberg (adoptive cell therapy and early gene-engineered TIL/TCR work). Eshhar and others are outside the supplied credit; this set is defensible but leaves some attribution questions around who made the foundational concept.
assessment.maturity: Approved products and long follow-up in B-cell malignancies; applicability to solid tumours remains limited and toxicity, relapse and access are open issues, but the core discovery is solidly established.
uncertainties: Foundational CAR concept credit (not all pioneers are in the supplied names)

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of a kinase inhibitor against the BCR-ABL driver turned CML from a fatal disease into a chronic manageable one; the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy with exceptionally clear clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery), Druker (clinical development and champion of trials), Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio. Rowley and Nowell/Hungerford and others earned prior recognition for the Philadelphia chromosome in other contexts, and the underlying translocation/ABL biology predates this work.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with two decades of survival data and replication across kinase-inhibitor classes. Recognition is not premature; the question is relative priority against other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the oncogene discoveries (BCR-ABL fusion) are considered the more fundamental discovery
Overlap with other previously honoured cancer-gene work

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING defined a general pathway by which cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity and type I interferon, connecting infection, autoimmunity (interferonopathies, lupus-like disease), cancer immunity and ageing. Highly original, mechanistically clear and of broad conceptual importance, including for my own field of autoimmunity.
assessment.attribution: Barber (STING identification), Chen (cGAMP second messenger and cGAS identification) are the decisive contributors; Ishikawa, Sun and Wu are important co-authors/early contributors. A two-person configuration is clean, though Barber and Chen are not the only possible pairing.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation, structural work and human genetic disease (STING-associated vasculopathy, Aicardi-Goutieres). Therapeutic translation is still early, so recognition would rest on mechanism rather than approved drugs.
uncertainties: Clinical therapeutic payoff not yet realized
Allocation of credit between STING discovery and cGAS/cGAMP work and contributors beyond two

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed that TNF is a pivotal driver in rheumatoid arthritis and that blockade is effective, establishing cytokine-targeted therapy and transforming outcomes in RA, IBD, psoriasis and other inflammatory disease. Clear, concrete and lasting impact. I note that this is within my clinical field and have judged it on the same criteria as others.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini are the clear academic leaders of the concept and the first clinical trials. Credit to others who cloned or developed TNF (e.g., Cerami, Beutler) and the biologic developers is outside this candidate's names.
assessment.maturity: Mature; decades of clinical use and biosimilars. Recognition is timely or even late, but this class has been a perennial candidate and its originality as an academic discovery relative to industrial development is debated.
uncertainties: Relative importance of the target-validation insight versus the therapeutic antibody development
Whether the prize would fairly represent others who contributed to TNF biology and anti-TNF antibodies

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing (nusinersen) converted spinal muscular atrophy from a lethal infantile disease into a treatable one and validated splice-switching oligonucleotides as a therapeutic class.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ASO target identification) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are a coherent pair. Others in SMN gene discovery (Melki, Lefebvre) and in splicing modulation also contributed, but are not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with multi-year clinical data; strong impact for a single disease and a class of RNA therapeutics, though breadth is narrower than other candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the SMN1 gene discovery should be recognized with the therapeutic work
Narrower disease scope compared with broad-impact candidates

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Discovery of the unfolded protein response and ER-to-nucleus signalling (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1) revealed a fundamental quality control and stress signalling principle with implications for diabetes, neurodegeneration, cancer and immunity.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently dissected the pathway; Walter's lab (with Cox) and Mori's work are the main credited contributors. Pairing is clear though others (Ron, Kaufman) contributed to the broader UPR.
assessment.maturity: Well established across yeast and mammals over three decades; disease relevance is emerging and mostly mechanistic rather than yielding approved therapies.
uncertainties: Credit among IRE1, ATF6 and PERK arms of the response

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Cloning of the T-cell receptor solved a central problem in immunology, the molecular basis of T-cell antigen recognition and the origin of its diversity, underpinning modern T-cell biology, immunotherapy and vaccines. Foundational and original.
assessment.attribution: Davis and Hedrick and Mak independently cloned TCR chains in 1984; Yanagi also contributed. Priority is shared and the three-name limit forces an exclusion of Yanagi. Authorship questions are genuine.
assessment.maturity: Long mature, completely validated; recognition is arguably late and the discovery has already been implicitly honoured via related prizes (MHC restriction, checkpoint therapy), which reduces urgency.
uncertainties: Priority and fair allocation among competing near-simultaneous cloning groups
Possible diminished novelty because later work built on and was recognised separately
